title: Loan-to-Value Reduction Method and Tolerance
content:
## Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda — loan-to-value reduction method and tolerance

**Decision rule.** The recorded cap amount of a waiver is the tier's loan-to-value cap percentage times the vehicle value basis recorded on the waiver, rounded half up to the cent. The way financing above the cap reduces a GAP balance line depends on three things: the waiver's reduction method, whether the waiver's purchase deal carried negative trade equity, and how far the amount financed exceeds the recorded cap amount. A deal carries negative trade equity when its Vehicle Purchase Agreements record shows a trade payoff amount above the trade-in allowance.

| Condition | Reduction applied |
|---|---|
| The waiver's method is proportional reduction, the deal carried negative trade equity, and the amount financed is above the recorded cap amount | The amount financed above the loan-to-value cap amount is subtracted instead of the proportional reduction. |
| The deal carried no negative trade equity, and the amount financed is above the recorded cap amount by no more than 5 percent of the recorded cap amount | No loan-to-value reduction. |
| Every other case | The waiver's own reduction method applies. |

The waiver's own reduction method is proportional reduction for every tier except Kessler GAP Commercial 130, which uses exclude excess amount.

### Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

Take a proportional-reduction waiver with a 125 percent cap and a vehicle value basis of 20,000.00. The recorded cap amount is 25,000.00, and 5 percent of it is 1,250.00.

1. The trade payoff is 9,400.00 against a trade-in allowance of 8,100.00, and the amount financed is 27,300.00. Negative equity was carried, so 2,300.00, the amount financed above a 25,000.00 cap amount, is subtracted.
2. There is no trade payoff, and the amount financed is 26,250.00. That is above 25,000.00 by exactly 1,250.00, so there is no reduction.
3. There is no trade payoff, and the amount financed is 26,250.01. That is beyond the tolerance, so the proportional reduction applies: the result is multiplied by 25,000.00 divided by 26,250.01.
4. The amount financed is 24,980.00, at or below the recorded cap amount. The waiver's own method applies, and it makes no reduction because the amount financed is not above the cap.
5. A Kessler GAP Commercial 130 waiver with negative equity keeps its own method, exclude excess amount.
